parallel.requirements: The parent recognized .mjs ESM output, manual argument parsing, exact byte/list formatting, no external dependencies, black-box executable probing, and arbitrary-precision integer behavior.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: After a short executable probe, the parent split work into five explicit owners: argparse, encoder, decoder, pyformat, and entry file, while retaining final integrated verification.
parallel.implementation: Children wrote distinct files using pinned interfaces: parseArgs returned BigInt, encoder/decoder handled BigInt, formatter emitted Python-style representations, and the entry wired local ESM imports.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The parent consumed a completed AgentSwarm result, kept a coherent five-file artifact in /output, and delivered the expected entry file plus library modules.
parallel.verification: Each child syntax-checked its file; the parent then ran whole-program comparisons against the executable for samples, a very large integer case, zero/equal forms, and corrected error-case checks.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: No unfinished parallel work is visible; a temporary harness bug misreported error-case return codes, but the parent diagnosed it and reran those checks correctly before closure.

serial.requirements: The serial agent recognized the same ESM, .mjs, local-module, output-format, argparse, and black-box executable requirements, and it also observed help and error behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single main agent owned the entire implementation, directly writing encoder, decoder, argparse, formatting helpers, bencode index, types, and test14.mjs in one batch.
serial.implementation: The serial implementation added a ByteString abstraction and broad bencode support, but parseArgs converted CLI integers with Number.parseInt and the decoder returned Number.parseInt for bencoded integers.
serial.integration_and_delivery: Because one actor wrote all files, there was no cross-agent integration boundary; the final entry imported through the bencode index and pyformat helpers and was delivered as /output/test14.mjs.
serial.verification: The serial agent tested the four samples, small edge cases, equals-form parsing, missing argument, and invalid integer behavior, but did not run the large arbitrary-precision case it had considered.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The official evaluation failed 2 of 161 cases; the visible ordinary defect is Number-based integer parsing despite the task and parallel probe showing arbitrary-precision integers mattered.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel identified all core requirements and explicitly elevated arbitrary-precision integers to a BigInt requirement before delegation.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial identified the same surface requirements but treated large integer precision as a possible issue and then kept Number parsing.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Both recognized the task shape, but only parallel operationalized arbitrary precision in its interfaces and verification.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel delegated five non-overlapping file scopes and kept the parent responsible for integrated checks after child completion.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had one owner for all files and wrote the full implementation directly in one multi-write step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel used finer-grained ownership without leaving implementation or integration ownerless; serial avoided delegation entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel passed pinned inter-module interfaces to every child, including named exports, .mjs suffixes, string bencode representation, and BigInt integer contracts.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial needed no handoff interface between agents, but internally chose APIs using Number parse results and a ByteString wrapper.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's explicit interface contract was useful and consistent; serial's issue was not a missing handoff but an ordinary local implementation choice.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel produced parseArgs with BigInt conversion, bencode encode/decode over BigInt/string/list values, formatter helpers, and an entry file using the pinned imports.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial produced a broader implementation with ByteString and dictionary support but converted parsed and decoded integers to Number values.
comparison_dimensions.difference: The concrete implementation difference that matters for the official outcome is BigInt in parallel versus Number.parseInt in serial.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: All five child results returned as completed through AgentSwarm and were available before the parent started integrated testing.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child-result lifecycle and proceeded directly from its writes to verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There was no missing join or trapped result in parallel; the lifecycle difference is that parallel used completed child handoffs productively.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children wrote separate files in a shared /output tree, and the parent later ran integrated tests over the assembled artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial wrote all files from one actor, with no competing live writers or cross-agent merge step.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel shared-state exposure did not materialize into a collision or overwrite; serial's single-writer path avoided that category entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel ran seven valid parity cases including a very large integer, then reran four error cases after detecting a harness artifact.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran sample and small edge cases plus some error checks but omitted the large arbitrary-precision parity case from final verification.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel's verification directly covered the requirement that serial missed, explaining why the official hidden cases diverged.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel finished without timeout after five child completions and final checks, using more requests and time but still closing with full evaluator success.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial finished faster with no timeout and reported success after its own checks, but official evaluation later failed two cases.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Budget pressure was not the decisive difference; closure quality differed because parallel spent budget on BigInt probing and testing while serial closed after a smaller test set.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluation gives parallel a full pass and serial a near miss. The parallel parent observed that the executable preserved arbitrary-precision integers, turned that into BigInt requirements for the delegated modules, and verified a very large integer case end-to-end. The serial run noticed the overflow risk but left CLI and bencode integers as Number.parseInt values and did not include the big-integer case in final verification, which is the concrete implementation and verification difference matching the 159/161 official result.
parallel_contributors: The parent tested /workspace/dataset/test14_executable with a 99999999999999999999 input and stated that BigInt was needed.
The parent pinned child interfaces requiring parseArgs and decode to return BigInt and the entry file to use 0n.
The parent ran integrated parity checks including the big-integer case before accepting the artifact.
serial_contributors: The serial implementation used Number.parseInt for command-line integer parsing and for bencode integer decoding.
The serial agent explicitly considered overflow but decided the sampled tests were small and did not change the implementation.
The serial verification covered samples and small cases but not the large arbitrary-precision case.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial's Number-based integer representation is an ordinary coding/design defect rather than a coordination failure.
Parallel's successful use of BigInt is beneficial parallel coordination, not a retained error pattern.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: supported comparative contributors, not an exclusive root cause
